metadata.title: PIRLS 2010/11 in New Zealand: An overview of findings from the third cycle of the Progress in International Reading Literacy Study (PIRLS)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report summarizes PIRLS-2010/11 results for New Zealand Year 5 students and compares them with other participating countries. It references PIRLS technical notes for sampling weights and generalising to the population, indicating that PIRLS uses a complex sampling design and weight-based estimation for country and subgroup statistics. The report does not provide the specific weight variable name(s) or replicate-weight method (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the excerpted text, but it explicitly points readers to the Technical Notes for “weighting” and sampling weights. Because this is a descriptive large-scale assessment reporting document (not an ML prediction study), the appropriate weighting approach is the one used in PIRLS scaling/estimation procedures as documented in the PIRLS technical documentation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is an overview/report of PIRLS achievement distributions, benchmarks, and contextual associations rather than an empirical ML analysis that models cognitive achievement using PV-based dependent variables. While PIRLS achievement scores are derived from IRT scaling and are typically reported on a PIRLS reading scale, the excerpt does not describe any PV generation/combining strategy for an analysis pipeline. Missing-data handling is discussed only at a high level (e.g., exclusions and response rates for contextual questionnaires), without specifying an imputation/deletion rule for an analytic model, so the specific missing-data handling strategy is not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report focuses on PIRLS-2010/11 Year 5 students in New Zealand. It states that approximately 5,600 Year 5 students from 192 schools participated in the main survey (and an additional field trial sample of about 880 from 30 schools in late 2009). It also notes that results exclude benchmarking participants and out-of-scope grades/countries, and that exclusions for students with limited proficiency in the test language and other participation criteria were applied according to PIRLS international guidelines; New Zealand’s exclusion rate is reported as 3.3% in 2010/11.

data.outcome_summary: PIRLS-2010/11 in New Zealand reports reading literacy achievement for Year 5 students (middle primary) and situates New Zealand’s results in an international context across 45 participating countries plus additional benchmarking participants. The assessment uses 10 reading passages (five literary, five informational) with multiple-choice and constructed-response items, and achievement is placed on a PIRLS reading scale anchored to a centrepoint of 500 (SD=100) using IRT-based scaling. The report highlights that New Zealand’s mean reading score (531) is significantly higher than the international scale centrepoint, with 45% reaching the High International Benchmark (550) and 14% reaching the Advanced International Benchmark (625). It also documents stability over time (no significant change in mean achievement from 2001 to 2010/11) and describes subgroup patterns by gender, ethnicity, home language, and school context. As a descriptive assessment report, it does not train or evaluate ML models, and it does not provide a PV-combining or missing-data imputation/deletion rule for an analytic prediction pipeline.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a PIRLS national overview report that synthesizes descriptive statistics, benchmark attainment, and contextual questionnaire findings rather than conducting an ML prediction/classification analysis. Consequently, there are no ML algorithms, no PV-handling strategy for a model-based dependent variable, and no empirical ML performance metrics to extract. The report also does not provide the specific missing-data handling rule for an analytic model, because it is primarily presenting PIRLS-estimated achievement and scale summaries.
